description: A multi-arm denylist regex is 'controlled' by negatives that each trip two or more arms; deleting an arm leaves the suite green.
example: atl_v0 geometry_ref: removing the decimal-pair and blank arms left all 3 geometry negatives red-as-expected and the suite green, while 'see 25.1, -80.4' now passed. Fixed: one negative per arm built to evade the others, plus per-arm sabotage (each removal reddens exactly its control).

description: ^…$ under Python re (jsonschema, linkml-validate) accepts 'value\n'; ECMA-262 does not. A YAML | block scalar produces exactly that.
example: atl_v0 sha256 and id patterns accepted '<64 hex>\n' in both declared validators. Fixed: (?!\n)$ on every anchored pattern + neg_sha256_trailing_newline.

recurrences.note: format.checksum '^sha256:…$' (and runspec STREAM_ID/DATE, board SHA) accepted a trailing newline; → \Z with negative cases

description: One control is declared to prove N sibling constraints ('same pattern shape'); the README claims all N while saying 'claimed only where a fixture proves it'.
example: atl_v0: one stream_id control for 5 id slots, one tag control for 7 enums, one evaluation control for closed-ness of all classes. Fixed: a control per sibling (ids, 6 enums, root + part closed-ness) or the claim downgraded to 'generator path, not controlled'.

recurrences.note: the atl_v0 README claimed interval deltas in [−1, 1] off one control (delta_lower ≥ −1) → neg_interval_upper_gt_1 and neg_interval_estimate_lt_minus1 added
required claims with no control (value negatives only) (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)

description: A fixture faithfully copies a source field whose pointer target is wrong; provenance discipline ('nothing from memory') propagates the error instead of catching it.
example: pos_exemplar limitations_ref copied '§12 Where the analogy breaks' from the board entry; the page numbers the section 11. Fixed in both (board entry note → generator fix at M-1d).

recurrences.note: a verbatim prose move carried 'the confident true positive with the longest lead' — a selection rule the code never implemented (it picks the most confident TP with lead >= 2).
F-6/F-7 (M-1d-i): 'a refusal writes nothing' copied into 3 documents while false; 'opens nothing under data/site' survived into contract v0.2.0

description: A perturbation self-test on dense, single-entity synthetic data cannot see defects that only exist with gaps (row-vs-calendar shift, bfill, observed-week horizon) or across entities (reshape order, station→unit mixing).
example: atlantis_core selftest v1 (one unit, 3 samples every week): a back-filled last-known state, a horizon counted in observed weeks, weeks-UNTIL-next-sample and a week-major table scramble all passed; on real data they moved positives 1168→949…1094 or scrambled 15,547 rows. Fixed: 2 patients (one isolable), gaps at t−4/t+2 (primary) and t−1/t (neighbour), daily week t−1, raw frames through normalise; 16 planted defects caught. Fix: Synthesise ≥ 2 entities and deliberate gaps around t; build through the real ingest path; plant each defect class and name the check that catches it.

recurrences.note: F-1 (M-1d-i): gap-dependent label defects invisible on the new daily event-stream shape

rectangle-only zones made a bounding-box mask indistinguishable (F-5), and no gap longer than last_known_weeks made raw vs carried refractory indistinguishable (F-7); → triangle/hole/MultiPolygon zones and an lk+1-week gap after a crossing, each with a plant
docs and tests knew three NDBC header forms; the record holds four; two guards unplanted (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)
the calm world held calm days only near the sine's zero-crossings; a March week left C0 nothing to remove (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: A window bound tested only from outside (t+H+1 must not move it) lets a shortened window pass. Test both edges: t+H must move it, and t+H alone must keep the outcome known.
example: atlantis_core selftest v1: a label looking H−1 weeks ahead passed C1 (t+1) and C2 (t+H+1); real data positives 1168→949, outcome-unknown drops 1800→2098. Fixed: C2b. Fix: For every window, one control just inside each edge and one just outside.

description: Leak invariance asserted on features and target but not on the ROW FILTERS (already-in-event, unknown-outcome) — the future leaks in through which rows are kept.
example: atlantis_core selftest v1: already_in_event = sig.shift(-1).ffill(4) passed; real data positives 1168→949, prevalence 0.108→0.088. Fixed: C1/C2/C3/C5 assert already_in_event unchanged at every week ≤ t. Fix: Treat every column that decides inclusion as a feature for leakage purposes.

recurrences.note: the trend baseline's leak tests covered s_t but not its sibling input s_prev; planting s_prev = shift(−1) (the step reads s(t+1)) left all 16 baseline tests green while the synthetic trend AUROC went 0.827 → 0.996 → plant S3 + s_prev ≡ the label's carried signal at t − 1 wk on every exemplar unit-week

description: Folding an imputer's missingness-indicator contribution into its vital's SHAP gives data availability (or unit identity) the vital's tag — a structurally-absent stream reads as a lever.
example: atlantis_core logistic swap: discharge_30d_t3 (lever) ranked #3 by mean|φ| 0.702, of which 0.708 came from its missingness flag (units 8/9 have no gauge); the T2 note then misread the top six. Fixed: flags are availability:<vital> pseudo-vitals tagged artifact, net group attribution reported beside abs-sums.

description: A control that cannot fail: additivity of a linear decomposition, refitting the same data, a guard flag set from argument presence, a denylist proven by its own three examples.
example: test_linear_shap_is_exact passed under any column→vital mapping; honoured = fold_tables is not None passed a no-op callable; assert_green passed a dict of 1,640 keyed predictions. Fixed: brute-force interventional φ per column, per-fold rebuild verified, allowlist + size/number caps, the reviewer's three as tests.

recurrences.note: a test named ..._sum_net passed with np.abs sums; board_check compared 5 of ~20 evaluated fields (a doctored Brier passed).
F-3b/F-5 (M-1d-i): tests asserted a one-word status flip ratifies, and an empty #limits section passes

M-1e: a fold check read selected_on, which the same code set from Y; planting fit(s_tr, te) and fold(Y) into the real loop left the suite green. check_thresholds_fixed's positive case used a rule that by signature could not see test. The producer's own first runtime fix recomputed the thresholds it compared against (caught before commit). Fixed: a FitRecorder proxy checks what fit() received; source-level plants P1-P4 into eval must fail by name.

the board's embargo guard walked headline, swaps and folds but not the ablation variants or the sensitivity run whose numbers it publishes under 'every boundary'; unembargoing either passed 76 tests and emitted → assert_embargo walks every variant and the sensitivity block; real-path plants Q2/Q3

assert_comparators was documented as arithmetic on the RESULT but holds by construction for the real eval (rate and positives/n from one frame); its plants were all result-dict mutations → documented as a tamper check; slot ↔ result equality added; the eval-time checks B1/B2 and plants S1–S3 are the controls

T9 weak form (no instance patch) holds by construction under the M-2 card's own 'stop, file the template change, do not patch locally' escalation rule — it measures that the process held, not that the method is drop-in.

the interval's pairing guard (idx_model, idx_comp = idx, idx; array_equal) could fail only under the plant that rewrote its own line; the identical-scores control was the real proof → guard dropped, C4 now planted against the identity control
probe_zero's control shows the source exists, labelled 'a true zero'; pass vacuous on both live runs
the calm-vital selftest plant was caught by C4's NaN check, never by C1, the check the test is named for (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)

description: A 'training-relevant' hash omits fields that choose which models are trained or which numbers the keyed record carries, and is stamped onto results it does not describe.
example: semantic_hash was unchanged under eval.ablations / sensitivity_threshold / vital group; the logistic swap file carried the xgboost-learner hash; lever_stations (what-if only) moved it. Fixed, each case a test.

recurrences.note: generalised to a cache key: the CRW per-zone cache omitted grid pin, pad and variable; → keyed by all three

the M-2a-i cache-key fix keyed three of the four basis fields and dropped base: a new base after a deleted artifact read the old source's spans (0 requests) under the new base's stamp; the generic ERDDAP cache keyed none → CRW key + base/zlev tag, ERDDAP basis subdir (base, variable, zlev, box); a plant without the base reproduces it

interval seed, draw count (and now season start month) sit outside semantic_hash — stamped on the result and entry, disclosed in the core README known limits; not added to the hash (it names the trained model, not its reading)

description: A control asserts the data a visual element needs, never that the element is drawn; the page's words then describe a mark that is not there.
example: Strips asserted split=None for excluded weeks; the template drew them as zero-width rects (x0 == x1 on a date axis), invisible since v0. Fixed: bands computed in Python as week-wide intervals and tested; checked rendered in a browser.

recurrences.note: conform item 10's new path read the page's embedded copy and passed a page whose script throws and draws nothing — the very defect the producer had just fixed (a // comment in a one-line IIFE killed every chart while 676 tests passed; found only in a browser) → item 10 needs the section renderer and a script that passes node --check (steward ruling 25); node --check test on the template

description: A build-time validator (Python) accepts what the runtime renderer (JS) cannot read: negative list indices, tokens in fields the renderer inserts verbatim, unknown format names, a figure id placed twice.
example: resolve('a.-1') passed; {{…}} in a section nav/strip label rendered literally; |pct rendered a raw float; a duplicated {{fig:pr}} gave duplicate DOM ids. Fixed: one grammar enforced on both sides, each case a planted test.

recurrences.note: the board validator (closed AtlEvaluation) did not constrain what the markdown renderer emits: newlines/'|' in limitations_ref and superseded_by wrote a heading onto BOARD.md; → closed top level, refuse control chars, escape '|'

description: A checker's hard-coded minimum is a strict subset of the template it guards, and its globs run on unnormalised paths, so the template's own protections can be deleted or walked around silently.
example: mapping --check passed with **/*.csv, site/**, geojson removed and with './data/…' as a source; edge_properties and json_properties were never checked; stamps were checked for presence, not value. Fixed: minimum = the template's fence, posixpath-normalised matching, edge/json/stamp-value checks, 11 more planted defects.

recurrences.note: F-3/F-5 (M-1d-i): posture check weaker than the ADR template's 4-field block; items 1/2/10/12 weaker than their rows

description: A check is extended to a new input shape, but the synthetic features that expose defects (gaps, edge cases) stay tied to the old shape, and the old shape's planted-defect suite is not re-run on the new one.
example: selftest let the event stream be daily (M-1d-i); the t+2 / neighbour-at-t gaps stayed point-only. in_event_bfill (a future leak into the row filter) and label_rowshift passed on both forked hypoxia instances while the exemplar caught them. Fixed: the event stream carries those gaps whatever its shape, and the whole 12-defect catalogue runs against two forked worlds.

recurrences.note: the year-window filter and weekly_count_lt's Obs branch were untested (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)
the centring was proved at a January week only; FKNMS's March week and a calm vital never ran (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: To fix a vacuity failure, a fallback moves the probe somewhere it cannot detect the defect it exists for. A loud refusal becomes a silent pass, and nothing reports the check that was lost.
example: gap_week moved the gap 'one past the span' when it hit a vital's lag; with lags {0,1,2} or {0,1} no gap lay between t−L and t, and a lag counted in rows passed. Fixed: C8 calendar-lag invariance (deleting (t−L, t] must not move a lag-L vital), and the run reports when C8 alone guards a stream.

recurrences.note: with the peer validator absent (every public clone) the lattice check exited 0 and its _graph silently dropped dangling edges; → local re-checks edge refs + duplicate ids, NOT RUN is printed

the C9 boundary probe was skipped on a condition broader than the carry it guarded (R+1 passed the whole self-test at R=4, iid), and the episode check returned 'not checked' without a word; → the gap week is filled and the probe always runs, an unrecomputable signal is refused, and C9's outcome is on the receipt

description: A check described as 'resolves inside X' is implemented as (root / p).is_file(). An absolute or ../ path satisfies it, so a gate can be met by a file outside X.
example: The fetch posture gate opened on Atlantis's own ratified ADR-000; conform item 7 passed on a sibling instance's ADR; fork wrote an absolute scratchpad path into units.yaml. Fixed: resolve() + is_relative_to(root), with ../ and absolute paths planted as tests.

description: A human-approval gate reads a one-word field an agent can edit (frontmatter status), while the document's real ratification is a signed block the gate never parses.
example: posture ADR: the dry run 'ratified' it by flipping status: proposed → ratified with the 4-field table still blank; the fetch CLI and conform item 7 (fetched) both passed. Fixed: parse the Ratification row (decision, ratified-by, ISO date, ratified) and require the frontmatter to agree.

recurrences.note: verbatim is not faithful; reviewed was not bound to the reviewed content (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)

description: A 'writes only its own X' gate tests a path that another flag can point anywhere, not the identity it protects.
example: board --entries: the outside-instance refusal checked that --outputs sat inside the entries' repo; --outputs pointed at the exemplar wrote Atlantis's board pairing one instance's config with another's metrics. Fixed: gate on the instance root, and require --outputs inside it.

recurrences.note: the board compared each boundary's window end against the record's own next_start, never the split; a boundary relabelled to guard 2021 emitted → expected years derived from inst.cfg.split

description: A hash/pin check runs only if the target exists, so a deleted or mistyped target turns the check into a silent pass.
example: datasets --check: deleting a grandfathered parquet or typo-ing its path left all three records ✅. Fixed: absent bytes the record promises are an error; otherwise a printed 'pin not verified' note.

description: 'A precedes B (a gate)' implemented as 'a path A→B exists' passes when a bypass edge is added; a gate needs dominance.
example: lattice: an added declarations→fetch edge skipped selftest and all three checks passed. Fixed: every source→fetch path must pass selftest (dominance), with the bypass edge planted.

description: A safety refusal fed by subprocess git output treats an error (no repo, wrong branch) as 'no evidence' and permits the act.
example: board --regenerate: origin/main hard-coded; in an instance repo on master the pushed entry was overwritten. Fixed: check return codes, read every remote-tracking ref, refuse when there is no repo/remote/upstream.

recurrences.note: run_controls.sh read grep exit 2 (a bad or option-like pattern) as 'all named': a REJECTS_ON starting with '-' left linkml-validate's reason test vacuous since 0.5.0, and the -e fix cured one cause only → rc read whole, 2 = instrument failure

description: A temporal-split check tests each row's timestamp, but the label reads t+1..t+H, so the last H steps of a fit or stop set are labelled by the held-out period.
example: M-1e check_fold_selection: stop year 2022 had 10 of 31 positives labelled by 2023 (test) onsets; the check passed by row year. Disclosed by operator ruling; embargo carded (idea_label_horizon_embargo).

description: A provenance field (threshold_from, selected_on) is written from the config's intent rather than from what the code did, and the gate reads only the field, so any defect beneath it emits clean.
example: M-1e lead_time threshold_from stamped from eval.threshold_from; a test-quantile lead threshold reproduced v1's 0.6818 under 'val' and board emit accepted it. Fixed: the lead time records alert_threshold; eval and the board check its identity with the fixed budget threshold, and realised = n_alerts / n_test by arithmetic.

recurrences.note: the CRW reduction block omitted the zone file / pad it was computed over, so a cache-first fetch after a re-pin emitted the old zones cleanly; → the basis (grid_sha256 · pad_deg · variable · base) is recorded and a different basis is refused by fetch, --verify and conform item 3

embargo_weeks documented as written 'from the boundaries it CHECKED' was the config-resolved E; a plant claiming 6 wk over 4-wk cuts emitted → reworded; the board requires rows_dropped ≥ the H-window crossing count
the summary's reduction.base came from the spec while the bytes came from a cache keyed without it, so the basis check passed on the old source's bytes

the board entry's config_bytes_md5 was stamped at run time and the config's board block was edited before the commit, so the entry named bytes no commit holds (the semantic hash did not move) → the board refuses an entry whose recorded bytes are not the file's; the entry re-issued as v2 (rulings 24, 26)
'count-only' probes: the NWIS arm read the full daily series; the 45/458 came from an unrecorded script
an offline re-reduction was labelled fetched_at_source 'fetch'; pipeline_version did not name the parser fix (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)

description: A per-entity loop keys caches, rows and records by an id the input format does not guarantee unique; duplicates collide silently.
example: CRW fetch keyed its cache and reduction by the zone id; a zone exported as two features with seg=5 hit the first feature's cache (wrong envelope, a fallback 1° away), wrote duplicate (seg, date) rows and overwrote the first record. Fixed: PolygonGrid, conform item 1 and fork refuse duplicate ids.

recurrences.note: conflicting duplicate timestamps kept by file order; a station listed twice duplicated its days (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)

description: Documentation states that config X makes module A agree with module B, no test pairs the two modules, and the claim is wrong — while the next mission is about to set X on its strength.
example: 'R = H makes the label's onset the one eval/lead.py counts' (docstring, schema slot, README, skill, test world): it is R = H − 1; R = H drops the only positive row of an onset H+1 weeks after the previous crossing. Fixed: doctrine corrected (operator ruling), tests/test_label_refractory.py pairs label.make with lead_time (coverage 1.0 at H−1, 0.5 at H).

recurrences.note: conform re-implemented the board's supersession while its comment said it read it (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)

description: A temporal boundary stated in calendar years is enforced in the binning's year (ISO-Monday weeks): the year's last bin holds days of the next calendar year, so the check is exact in bins while prose claims calendar years.
example: M-1f embargo: exact in week-years; under a calendar-date perturbation 1 kept training and 5 kept validation labels read 1–5 January (the 2019-12-30 week). Fixed: README 2b states the convention; a raw-stream perturbation test binned as the label is.

recurrences.note: the interval's "season" block was the calendar year (week.dt.year); two of four K. brevis test blooms straddle New Year → ruling 5: season_start_month (exemplar August), partial edge seasons disclosed

description: A leakage check re-derives the label window from the same helper the cut uses, and no test perturbs the labeller's own input — a shared off-by-one would pass both cut and check.
example: M-1f: embargo() and check_label_windows() both use _window_end; only hand-pinned counts guarded them. Fixed: tests/test_embargo_perturbation.py inflates raw event observations past each boundary, rebuilds through label.make — 0 kept labels move, every dropped one does, a cut one week short leaks. Related C-006, C-025.

description: A wait loop or gate tests a cheap proxy for availability (an index page answering 200) instead of the real operation at its real size, so it waits on a condition that can never make the operation succeed.
example: M-2a-ii: a probe-gated fetch loop ran 39 attempts over ~2¼ h on index.html=200 while CRW's proxy cut every request at ~10.3 s and a 5-year chunk took ~40 s — futile by construction. Found by timing requests against chunk size (2 d 0.5 s → 1 yr >10 s); fixed by 15-day union spans (core 0.5.2). Related C-023.

description: A completeness claim is made by counting nulls in the rows that arrived, which cannot see rows that never arrived.
example: M-2a-ii: FKNMS DHW 'no nulls' over 1985-03-25→2025-12-31 read as complete; 1999-05-01 is absent for all 21 zones (CRW's own axis). Fixed: provenance.daily_completeness (distinct days vs calendar span, dates_per_unit) in ERDDAP/CRW summaries; fetch --verify prints ⓘ; the instance discloses the gap (steward ruling 17).

description: A descriptive drift is recorded with an untested cause stated as fact, where confounders in the data's own provenance are known and unexcluded.
example: M-2a-ii: 'the train→test base-rate rise is warming itself' (instance STATE, AAR) while CoralTemp's 2002 input change (the OSTIA residual its posture ADR discloses) and DHW's fixed MMM climatology were not separated. Fixed: 'consistent with warming; not separated from …'. SO-4/SO-9 neighbour.

recurrences.note: T4's FKNMS note attributed calibration slope 1.99 to the base-rate shift 'the stopping rule did not cause'; a prevalence shift moves calibration-in-the-large more than slope, and the AUPRC-stopping arm was not run.
a failed anemometer (LONF1 2020, 0.14–0.20×) was called 'drift' in STATE (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)
"the rise was composition" outran a table where the ruled share still rises 4.6 → 5.5 and the mean falls (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: A threshold-free precision metric (AUPRC) is compared across labels or row sets with different prevalence and read as inflation or improvement, with no lift, base-rate normalisation, or a comparator measured on the same rows.
example: M-2b T3: persistence-inclusive label AUPRC 0.929 vs onset 0.690 read as 'inflation' — prevalence 0.270 vs 0.150 and 7,644 vs 5,595 test rows; the model's lift fell 4.60 → 3.44. The honest signal: the no-model persistence comparator closing on the model (52% → 88% of its AUPRC). Fixed: lift reported; falsifier restated so prevalence cannot meet it.

description: A status roll-up line (register summary, AAR headline, STATE) claims more support than the rows it summarises say.
example: M-2b: the thesis register's 'Reading' line listed T3 and T10 as supported-by-two-instances while T3's row said the exemplar run was not repeated and T10's row said one instance-sourced entry. Fixed: 'tested on one instance (FKNMS)'.

recurrences.note: T9's 'nine' omitted the M-2a-i set the pre-fork survey forced and counted M-2a-ii's III fixes but not M-2b's (two counting rules); BOARD.md 'Lead (budget)' prints '1.0 of 105 … (@ 0.1)' at a threshold that flagged 20.3% of test.
the instance STATE kept 'the margin is mostly AUPRC' and entry v2 after the page was corrected; the register's 'every other row stands' skipped T9's +1 (F-8)
'identical' stated without the limit that the agent knew the registry it reproduced
the T8/T12 readings and rank 1 strength said more than the rows (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)
"v4 is written under 2ba2d4f939" — the vitals and the constant move the hash (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: A register promises a test to a phase or mission; the re-card copies acceptance from the old card, not from the register, and the test silently disappears.
example: P2: T2's 'swap on a second instance (M-2)' was absent from M-2a and M-2b (FKNMS learner_swaps empty); T4's 'P2 replication' ran no AUPRC-stopping arm. Fixed at the P2 gate: each carried, dropped or recorded in the ruling; M-2c and the P3 cards carry register obligations explicitly.

description: A claim is called supported on evidence measured at a different operating point than its own falsifier names.
example: T11's falsifier is 'does not beat its climatology at the chosen budget'; only threshold-free AUROC/AUPRC existed on either instance, yet the status read 'supported' from M-0. Fixed at the P2 gate: T11 → untested at its terms; climatology-at-budget carded in M-2c.

recurrences.note: uncertainty off the falsifier's operating point again: the M-2c-i interval covered threshold-free AUROC/AUPRC only, while T11 names the budget; precision at budget was a point estimate at unequal realised rates → ruling 3: Δ precision/recall at the fixed thresholds and a matched-volume Δ precision in the same paired draws

T11 measured at its operating point, then read off it in prose: 'the chosen budget' read at the volume a validation-fixed threshold delivered under the shift (20.3%), not the volume a steward staffs; the verdict led with a raw precision gap at unequal volumes
rank strength counted rows whose event is not the instance's (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)

description: A suite is reported green at one commit, and a later commit in the same mission (a data or board entry the tests read live) turns it red. The recorded count names no commit, so the claim outlives the state it described.
example: M-2c-i: 731 passed at 0da7414; 6fa20d3 landed board v4, and test_board_index::test_f9_supersession_is_derived (which hard-codes v3 as the stem's top) fails, 730/731 at HEAD.

recurrences.note: 590f70b pinned the site test's streams but still read the live features.yaml and metrics.json (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)

description: A bootstrap interval is printed with its nominal level (0.95) when there are too few resampling units for that level to be delivered. A percentile bootstrap over B blocks under-covers badly at small B, so 'does not span 0' is read as significance the sample cannot give. This is the interval counterpart of a nominal alert budget printed without its realised rate.
example: M-2c-i: 4 season blocks (35 multisets); simulated coverage ≈ 0.80 at B = 4 and ≈ 0.87 at B = 7. 'Spans 0: no' ≡ all 4 seasons favour the model (sign test p = 1/16), yet BOARD printed '0.95: [+0.11, +0.48] … no'.

description: A guard verifies a variable computed beside the operation's input, not the very object the operation consumes. A defect introduced between the check and the use, or at the call site, passes the guard and every planted-defect test written against the checked line. Kin to C-018 (proxy, not identity) and C-023 (label, not the act).
example: M-2c-i: assert_whole_blocks(idx) while scoring reads idx_model/idx_comp (a row resample after the check passes); check_label_windows(sel) while climatology_scores(train, val) is what ran (an unembargoed fit passes).

recurrences.note: the page's 'field for field' board_check compared `evaluation` only, while 8255d9b let the page cite `evaluation_extras.paired_interval` — a doctored matched-volume estimate passed
server_count range-only on ERDDAP and count-only on NWIS; probe_zero control proves existence; samples_per_year counted from the chosen min_train_year
"verified verbatim" was stronger than its guard; the 25-word cap guarded one field (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)

description: One document reads one comparison through an interval ('cannot be told apart') and a sibling comparison off point estimates ('X is better'), with the same instrument available for both. The verdicts then differ in rigour, not in evidence.
example: M-2c-ii register: T11's model − climatology ΔP −0.0221 [−0.09, +0.07] is read as 'cannot be told apart', while T2's logistic − GBM Δ AUROC +0.0095 (no interval; reviewer's season-block approximation [−0.006, +0.025], 6 of 7 seasons) is read as 'the simpler learner is the better one'.

description: A procedure, page or commit message justifies a property by naming a guard, but the guard checks a weaker or neighbouring property. The documented safety outruns the code, and a defect inside the gap passes the guard and the citation alike. Kin to C-037 (the guard reads a sibling of the consumed input) and C-023 (the label, not the act).
example: M-2c-ii: 'commit atlantis.yaml before the run; core refuses stale config bytes', where assert_config_bytes compares the run md5 to the working tree at emit time, not to a commit. 'The build checks the page against the entry field for field', where board_check compares the `evaluation` block only, while the page cites evaluation_extras.paired_interval (a plant passes).

recurrences.note: the delta_vs bucket bounds a count; nothing verifies an echo equals a board value
the cache was trusted, not verified against its manifest hash (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)
a plant cited for one check was caught by another; a fix claimed beyond its reach (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)
the mask was placed under "every operation looks only backward" while its flag reads 7 days ahead (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: A human ruling that accepts a failing check is keyed by the check's name, not by the failure it was given for. Any later, different failure of the same check is silently accepted, and the gate exits clean. The ruling's prose names the specific evidence, but the code never binds it. Kin to C-037 (the guard reads a sibling) and C-017 (the gate reads an agent-writable status).
example: M-3a: discover's apply_rulings turns any longitude_by_unit fail into 'accepted' because a ruling exists for the trap. The ruling names units 2, 3 and 8. A plant moving 49% of unit 4 offshore was accepted with exit 0. The server_count ruling for USGS 02359170 would equally accept an FWC layer drift.

description: A re-run in a weaker mode (offline, unprobed, or a subset) writes to the same path as a richer committed record. It overwrites it without a check, so the working record loses evidence (probe counts, accepted rulings) and nothing warns. Statuses that were 'accepted' become 'na', and the unused ruling is visible only in a machine file.
example: M-3a: runspec plans `discover --instance I --compare …` with the default --out <instance>/discovery. Run on the exemplar, it would replace the committed probed memo (server_count accepted, the 02359170 evidence) with an offline one (server_count, probe_zero and negative_flow all na). render_md never prints ruling_unused.

recurrences.note: a --refresh during an outage would overwrite the corpus record (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)

description: A mission card's budget tripwire ('> +50% → SITREP and stop; re-card') is recorded only after the work is done. The operator never gets the stop-or-continue decision the tripwire exists to give, and the card's estimate and scope are not re-cut. Lanes folded in mid-sitting are what push the budget over the line.
example: M-3a: about 306 kT against a trip of about 210 kT. The SITREP is the session log's last bullet, after all seven commits. The card's budget and scope were not amended for the folded GREEN-cap and CEL lanes. Precedent outside the store: the M-1c AAR says 'A SITREP at the trip point was still owed and was not given'.

recurrences.note: SITREP came ~55 kT past the +50% line; the reader lane had no budget line (frequency bump accepted by the operator, 2026-10-12)
SITREP ≈ 65 kT past the +50% line; the re-card (ruling 7) was not on the card (operator ruling 10, 2026-10-12)
the counter was not read at 2e4f8dd; the +50% line was probably crossed unseen (operator ruling 8, 2026-10-16)

description: A slot claimed 'required, non-blank' (or a range claimed at both ends) is 'controlled' only by negatives on the value: blank, unknown enum value, below the minimum. No fixture omits the key or crosses the other bound, so deleting `required` or the maximum leaves every world green. A catch by side effect (an optional inlined object emitted anyOf [object, null], so a sibling negative fails as an unnamed branch) shows in some worlds only and is not a control. Kin to C-006 (one-sided window) and C-003 (proof by analogy).
example: M-3b-i atl_v0 0.9.0: removing `required` one slot at a time left all three worlds green on 16 AtlHypothesis slots, including realisable_as (T8's column), mechanism, driver_direction, result and year. `realisation` and `driver_lag` reddened only the two JSON worlds, via unnamed anyOf branches, while linkml-validate stayed 103/103. `year`'s maximum 2100 was unproven (only 201 < 1800 had a control). The README row claimed all of these. Fix: one neg_<class>_without_<slot> per claimed required slot, a negative for each range bound, and the required-removal sweep recorded as instrument proof.

description: A single reader applies a written review rule ('withdraw a row resting on background framing'; 'a phrase like "related to" gives no sign: no row') to some rows and not to others carrying the same defect. The rule is then hardened into the skill, but nothing re-runs it over the rows already kept, so the ledger keeps exceptions its own skill forbids, some of them promoted.
example: M-3b-i coral_reef: wind_002 was withdrawn as background framing, while amo_002 (a context sentence in a coral-growth SST reconstruction) was confirmed `reviewed`. Skill step 3 lists 'related to' as giving no sign, yet enso_002 ('related to … respectively') was kept. Fix: when a rule enters the skill, re-run it over every existing row, mechanically (grep the trigger phrases) or with a second reader, and record the outcome per row.

description: A data sanity or agreement check (stations agree, the index is defensible) is run on a window chosen for completeness, such as the years when every source reports. That window excludes the period the model is scored on. A fault confined to the scored window passes, and the roll-up line names what it did see with a cause ('drift'), which absorbs the fault.
example: M-3b-ii-a FKNMS reef-light wind: 'daily r 0.87-0.95 between lights (2000-15, all four reporting) - the synoptic index is defensible'. LONF1 read at 0.14-0.20 x the other lights from 2020-02-27 to 06-04 (a failed anemometer: 2020 annual mean 2.72 vs ~5.2, with stuck-at-zero runs), inside the 2019-25 test window. STATE called it 'LONF1 drifts calmer too'. It inflates test calm days at c = 3-6 by +27 to +51. Fix: run the read per segment, test included, and per station x year; add a QC flag (ratio to the others' median, identical-value runs) before any vital reads the stream.

description: Rows sharing a key (timestamp, id) are deduplicated with keep-first and counted as 'duplicates', with no check whether the duplicated records agree. A conflicting record, such as another source's data filed under this key, is resolved by file order, and the summary cannot tell a benign repeat from a collision. The only test builds the benign case. Kin to C-024 (entity id assumed unique).
example: M-3b-ii-a NDBCStdmet: SMKF1 2020 holds 653 within-file timestamps (06-01 to 06-05) with two different records. The second is LONF1's record (hourly r 0.999). drop_duplicates(keep='first') kept the true-looking block only because it came first, and the summary reported duplicates: 869 as benign. The docstring speaks only of cross-year-file duplicates. Fix: count identical and conflicting duplicates separately; refuse, or drop both and count, a conflicting key unless a rule says which source wins; plant a within-file conflicting block.

description: A fetcher records a source as 'absent' (a 404, an empty subset) from a single reply, with no retry, and caches that as a zero-byte file that any later run reads as permanent absence. An empty successful reply is indistinguishable from it. Absence is a record the method reports as fact (years_absent), so a transient error, or a period the source has not yet published, becomes data. Kin to C-021 (git probe fail-open) and C-019 (pin check skips on an absent target).
example: M-3b-ii-a NDBCStdmet: _absent = status 404, short-circuiting the retry loop. The cache is a zero-byte file, and `data or None` treats any empty file as absent. In plants, an empty-body 200 was recorded in years_absent, and a one-off 404 survived a later run against a healthy server (0 requests). A spec extended to the current year would make NDBC's not-yet-published yearly file 'absent' forever. The raw cache carries no per-file hash or time, so 'bytes equal after an offline re-reduction' proves determinism, not the cache. Fix: an .absent.json sidecar (status, time, URL); an empty 200 fails; confirm a 404 after a backoff; refuse years reaching the current year; record a per-file sha256 and fetched_at.

description: A planted-defect test asserts only the error type (pytest.raises(LeakError)). Its plant trips an unrelated check, such as a vacuity or NaN guard, before the check the test is named for runs. The test is green and the commit says the instrument catches the defect, but the target check was never exercised on it. A plant that evades the side check might, or might not, be caught. Kin to C-009 (control true by construction) and C-015 (fallback relocates the probe).
example: M-3b-ii-a test_selftest_passes_with_a_calm_vital_and_catches_a_future_read: the shift(-1) plant (next week's calm count) was caught by C4 ('vitals NaN at (primary, t)', because week t+1 is a synthetic gap), and at lag 1 by C0, never by C1. Plants that keep t non-NaN (count_t + count_t+1; next week, else own week) were caught by C1 LEAK, so the instrument works but the test does not show it. Fix: a plant that leaves the baseline valid, and assert the specific check by message (match='C1 LEAK').

description: A leakage self-test perturbs a stream's value column after t and checks nothing at or before t moves. A derived column precomputed at fetch (a QC flag, a rolling statistic) then enters the vitals beside the value, through a new path, but the synthetic world fills it with a constant and the test never perturbs it. A derived column computed with a centred window reads the future, and the instrument cannot fail on it. The documentation still says every operation looks only backward. Kin to C-039 (guard cited for a stronger property) and C-005 (degenerate synthetic fixture).
example: M-3b-ii-b-1: mask_columns applies NDBCStdmet's qc_low_ratio (a centred 15-row rolling median, ndbc.py:315) to the value before any op. The self-test sets every flag False (selftest.py:273) and perturbs only value, so C1 cannot see a flag that reads t+1. On FKNMS, centred and trailing flags differ on 6 station-days (LONF1 2020-02-27…, test). Fix: compute the masking flag causally, or report it as a declared exception; have the self-test perturb every mask column after t.

description: A config section whose keys switch behaviour on (a mask, an offset, a window) is validated only for the keys the checker knows. An unknown or misspelled key is neither refused nor read: the config loads green, the hash moves (it covers the section), and the behaviour silently does not happen. The same openness lets an older engine load a newer config under the same hash and ignore the new keys. Kin to C-019 (pin check skips on absent target) and C-043 (presence claim controlled only by value negatives).
example: M-3b-ii-b-1: a FKNMS copy with 'mask_column:' and 'station_offset:' loaded with no error (hash 6b167519f6), with no mask and no offsets applied. Core 0.10.1 loads the 0.11.0 FKNMS config with the same semantic hash 2ba2d4f939 and ignores all three keys. Fix: R5 refuses unknown stream-spec keys (closed set per shape), with a did-you-mean; plant a misspelled key.

description: Whether a planted-defect check can fail depends on a parameter chosen for another reason (the test week, a seed, a season), not on the defect. A fix that makes the instrument bite is validated at one value of that parameter (the variant's week). The parameter is then moved in the instance to satisfy a different guard, and the instrument goes blind or red there for the world's fault. Re-picking the parameter until the check passes would choose it by the outcome. Kin to C-005 (degenerate synthetic fixture), C-014 (generalised input keeps old-shape fixture) and C-048 (plant caught by an unrelated check).
example: M-3b-ii-b-1: the weekly_count_lt-centred synthetic world puts unit-level values near the threshold only near the sine's zero-crossings. selftest.week moved 2014-01-06 → 2014-03-03 to clear the offset era; with ii-b-2's calm vitals, FKNMS fails C0 at every c in {2..6} in March, and passes in July or October. The core test proving the centring ran a January week. Fix: a season-proof world plus an assertion that each perturbed week holds 1–6 calm days ('world fault' by name); never move the week to make C0 pass.

description: Station QC, windows, offsets or other preprocessing are chosen after inspecting a covariate over every segment, validation and test included. No label or model output is read, so it is not label leakage, but the test score is no longer independent of the preprocessing choices. Nothing in the limits, the card or the board entry says so. A diagnostic at a coarse resolution (yearly means) then fixes a ruling whose premise a finer one (deseasonalised months) contradicts. Kin to C-045 (agreement-check window excludes scored window) and C-030 (descriptive shift given causal label).
example: M-3b-ii-b-1: rulings 1, 2 and 4 on the FKNMS wind index were made on the LONF1 failure found in test, SMKF1's post-gap shift (val/test years, costing 123 test days) and a val residual of −0.3 that triggered ruling 4, chosen from yearly paired differences over 1988–2025. The ii-b-2 limits (a)–(e) do not disclose it. Monthly, deseasonalised differences put SANF1's 'May 2006' step after Sep 2006, completing after a second outage in 2007. Fix: a limit 'ruled label-blind on the full covariate record'; give break diagnostics in months.
